Prerequisite

/pree-REK-wuh-zit/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Prerequisite means something that is required as a prior condition before something else can happen or exist

Prerequisite means something that is required as a prior condition before something else can happen or exist. Passing the written traffic exam is a prerequisite for earning a learner's permit.

Worked Example

Passing the pool's swim test is a prerequisite for joining the kayaking class, so no one touches a paddle until they can tread water for two minutes.

The swim test must be completed before the class is even allowed to begin. A condition that comes first and unlocks what follows is a prerequisite.

How Prerequisite Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

requirement

requirement: something that must be met or done

precondition

precondition: a condition that must exist beforehand

qualification

qualification: a skill or credential needed for something

Antonyms

option

option: something you are free to choose or skip

luxury

luxury: something pleasant but not needed

How Strong Is It? — suggestion → necessity → prerequisite

suggestion vs. prerequisite

suggestion vs. prerequisite: Suggestion is weaker: a suggestion can be ignored, but a prerequisite must be met before you can move forward at all.

necessity vs. prerequisite

necessity vs. prerequisite: Necessity is stronger and broader: a necessity is required no matter what, while a prerequisite is required specifically before a particular next step.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — pre-

Prefix — pre-: before, in advance (Latin prae-)

Root — requisite

Root — requisite: required, sought after (Latin requirere, from quaerere, to seek or ask)

Put it together

Put it together: Pre- (before) + requisite (required, from Latin requirere): a prerequisite is something required before the next step can happen.

Use the root in a new word: query

Use the root in a new word: query: He sent a polite query to the librarian, seeking the title of the town's oldest map.

Word Choice

Academic / formal

Standard in course catalogs and job postings, usually followed by 'for': 'a prerequisite for enrollment.' It can also act like an adjective, as in 'a prerequisite course.'
